label: Google Slides
description: Arcade.dev LLM tools for Google Slides

tools.name: CommentOnPresentation
tools.description:
Add a comment to a presentation, or reply within an existing comment thread.

Comments are file-level, not anchored to a slide; to reference a slide, name it in
the text. Pass reply_to_comment_id to post within that thread instead of starting a
new comment.

parameters.name: presentation_id
parameters.description: The id of the presentation to comment on.

parameters.name: comment_text
parameters.description: The comment text to add.

parameters.name: reply_to_comment_id
parameters.description: Post the text as a reply within an existing comment thread by passing that comment's id. Leave empty to start a new top-level comment.

comment_text.value: Please review slide 3 — the Q3 revenue chart needs updated figures before we present.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: CreateOrEditPresentation
tools.description:
Create a deck or apply a batch of edits to one, returning created object ids,
replace counts, and a fresh addressable snapshot.

Use this single tool for all deck construction and editing: add, delete, or restyle
slides and elements, insert and replace text, and brand a deck in one batch. Reorder
slides with an updateSlidesPosition request; duplicate a slide or element with a
duplicateObject request. To set speaker notes, insertText into a slide's
notes_object_id (surfaced per slide in the snapshot).

To add a slide into a specific branded layout, first read the deck and consult the
snapshot's layout inventory: each layout reports its placeholders (type, index, and
object id), so you can pick a layout that already carries the title/body/other
placeholders you intend to fill rather than guessing which layout holds what, and
address a specific placeholder in placeholderIdMappings (by {type, index} or by
layoutPlaceholderObjectId) even when a layout repeats a type. Read the snapshot to
discover the object ids later edits target.

The batch is atomic: one invalid request rejects the whole batch, so target object
ids that exist in the snapshot. Object ids you assign to new objects are validated
before the batch is sent.

parameters.name: requests
parameters.description: Ordered batchUpdate requests to apply. Each item sets exactly one request key. Pass an empty list to create a blank deck or to re-read an existing one. Any caller-chosen objectId (on createSlide, createShape, createTable, etc.) must be 5-50 characters long and contain only letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, or colon, beginning with a letter, digit, or underscore; it must be unique within the batch and the deck. These ids are validated before the batch is sent.

parameters.name: presentation_id
parameters.description: Omit to create a new deck; provide a deck id to edit that deck in place.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Title for a newly created deck. Ignored when editing an existing deck.

parameters.name: keep_default_slide
parameters.description: When creating a new deck whose requests add their own slides, the blank slide Google auto-creates is removed so the deck contains only what you built. Set true to keep that auto-created blank first slide. Ignored when editing an existing deck or when no new slides are created. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: snapshot_detail
parameters.description: How much per-slide detail the returned snapshot carries. OUTLINE reports object ids, placeholders, text, and notes; FULL adds per-element geometry. Defaults to OUTLINE.

parameters.name: include_layouts
parameters.description: Include the deck's layout inventory in the returned snapshot. Omit to use the default, which includes layouts when creating a new deck (their object ids are needed to add slides into branded layouts) and omits them when editing an existing deck (where layouts rarely change between edits and only add tokens). Set true or false to force.

parameters.name: include_masters
parameters.description: Include the deck's master inventory in the returned snapshot. Masters rarely change between edits and are the heaviest part of the snapshot, so they are omitted by default; set true when verifying a master-level branding edit.

parameters.name: return_slide_ids
parameters.description: Scope the returned snapshot's slides to these slide object ids (in deck order). Omit (null) to return every slide; pass an empty list to return no slides (the snapshot still reports slide_count and other deck-level fields). Use after a localized edit to get back only the slides you touched instead of the whole deck.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: CreatePresentationFromTemplate
tools.description:
Derive a new on-brand deck from an existing branded deck, preserving its
masters, layouts, and theme, then optionally filling tokens.

Use this instead of building from scratch when the user wants a deck in their
company template; the new deck inherits the source's branding.

parameters.name: source_presentation_id
parameters.description: The id of the branded deck to derive the new deck from.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Title for the new deck.

parameters.name: text_replacements
parameters.description: Token replacements applied to the new deck after copying (e.g. fill {{COMPANY}} with a value). Omit for a verbatim brand copy.

parameters.name: match_case
parameters.description: Whether token matching is case-sensitive. Defaults to true.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GenerateGoogleFilePickerUrl
tools.description:
Generate a URL where the user grants this app access to specific Drive files.

Check `status` first. "unavailable" is not an error: either this app already reaches
every presentation the connected account can open, so there is no per-file grant to
request, or the picker is not configured here. Either way `reason` explains it, no URL
exists, and a presentation that could not be read is one the account itself cannot
open. Do not retry it.

On "available", use this when a prior tool reported a file was not found or access was
denied and the user expects the file to exist; after the user completes the picker,
retry the prior tool. Opens Google's first-party Drive picker, not a sign-in prompt.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetPresentation
tools.description:
Return an addressable snapshot of a deck: slide and element object ids,
placeholder types, text, speaker notes, and the layout and master inventory.

This is the read side of the read-edit loop: the object ids it returns are the
addresses create_or_edit_presentation targets. Each layout in the inventory
reports its placeholders with type, index, and object id, the identity a
createSlide placeholderIdMappings entry needs (by {type, index} or by
layoutPlaceholderObjectId), even when a layout repeats a placeholder type.

What this response leaves out is reported in words by next_step, which is empty only
when nothing was left out: read it before answering anything about slides it does not
contain.

parameters.name: presentation_id
parameters.description: The id of the presentation to read.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: OUTLINE reports object ids, placeholders, text, notes, and the layout/master inventory. FULL adds per-element geometry. Defaults to OUTLINE.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed first slide to return. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: max_slides
parameters.description: Maximum slides to return in this read (1-50). Defaults to 50; use offset to page.

parameters.name: include_layouts
parameters.description: Include the layout inventory. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: include_masters
parameters.description: Include the master inventory. Defaults to true.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetSlideThumbnail
tools.description:
Render one slide to a PNG. By default this returns a short-lived content
URL and pixel size. Set include_image to get the PNG as a data URI so you
can visually confirm layout, overflow, and branding before sharing.

Use this after creating or editing a slide when you need a preview, not
when you only need object ids or text. data_uri is omitted unless
include_image is true; it is a PNG in the form data:image/png;base64,...
Prefer SMALL or MEDIUM when including the image; LARGE occupies more of
the context window.

parameters.name: presentation_id
parameters.description: The id of the presentation.

parameters.name: slide_object_id
parameters.description: The object id of the slide (page) to render, from a read.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Rendered size: LARGE (~1600px), MEDIUM (~800px), or SMALL (~200px). SMALL is enough to check layout; LARGE is for reading small text and costs more context. Defaults to MEDIUM.

parameters.name: include_image
parameters.description: When true, the response includes data_uri (the PNG as data:image/png;base64,...) so you can visually inspect the slide. Defaults to false because the encoded image is large; set true only when you need to see the slide.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListPresentationComments
tools.description: List a page of comments and their replies on a presentation, newest first.

parameters.name: presentation_id
parameters.description: The id of the presentation to list comments for.

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Include deleted comments. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum comments to return per page (1-100). Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Cursor for the next page, taken from a prior response's next_page_token. Leave empty to fetch the first page.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ResolveComment
tools.description:
Close (resolve) or reopen a comment thread on a presentation.

Posts an action reply on the thread, so the lifecycle change is attributed to the
connected account; the thread's existing comments and replies are preserved.

parameters.name: presentation_id
parameters.description: The id of the presentation the comment is on.

parameters.name: comment_id
parameters.description: The id of the comment thread to resolve or reopen.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Whether to resolve (close) the thread or reopen a resolved one. Defaults to RESOLVE.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: SearchPresentations
tools.description:
Search the user's Drive for presentations, newest first by default.

Keyword matching is full-text: a keyword matches a deck's body content as well
as its title, so a deck can match on words that never appear in its title. A
keyword search that matches nothing returns an empty list (not an error).

An empty list is only a definitive no-match when next_step is empty. When next_step is
set, the listing was not walked to its end and the pages it did not reach may hold the
match, so do not report that no such presentation exists from that response alone.

parameters.name: presentation_contains
parameters.description: Keywords that must appear in the presentation title or content. Omit to list all.

parameters.name: presentation_not_contains
parameters.description: Keywords that must NOT appear in the presentation title or content.

parameters.name: search_only_in_shared_drive_id
parameters.description: Restrict the search to this shared drive. Omit to search across the user's drives.

parameters.name: include_shared_drives
parameters.description: Include presentations from shared drives. Defaults to false (My Drive only).

parameters.name: include_organization_domain_presentations
parameters.description: Include organization-wide presentations (admin accounts only). Defaults to false.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sort order. Defaults to most recently modified first. Ignored when a keyword filter is provided.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum presentations to return (1-100). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: Token from a prior result's next_page_token to fetch the next page.

tools.description: Return the connected Google account's profile (name, email, picture).

summary:
## Google Slides Toolkit

The Google Slides toolkit connects Arcade to the Google Slides (and Drive) APIs, enabling LLMs to create, read, edit, and comment on presentations programmatically.

## Capabilities

- **Deck creation and editing:** Create presentations from scratch or from branded templates, apply atomic batches of structural and content edits (add/delete/restyle slides and elements, insert/replace text, reorder slides, set speaker notes), and derive new decks from existing masters and themes.
- **Reading and inspection:** Retrieve fully addressable snapshots of a deck—slide/element object IDs, placeholder types, text, speaker notes, and layout/master inventories—and render individual slides to PNG thumbnails (URL or base64 data URI) for visual verification.
- **Search and discovery:** Full-text search across a user's Drive presentations (title and body content), with pagination support.
- **Comments and lifecycle:** Add top-level comments or threaded replies on presentations, list existing comments and replies, and resolve or reopen comment threads.
- **File access and identity:** Generate a Google Drive inline file picker URL to request per-file access when a presentation is inaccessible, and retrieve the connected account's profile (name, email, picture).

## OAuth

This toolkit authenticates via OAuth 2.0 using Google as the provider. See the [Arcade Google auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/google) for setup details.

## Secrets

- **`ENABLE_GOOGLE_DRIVE_INLINE_PICKER_URL`** — Controls whether the `GenerateGoogleFilePickerUrl` tool is active. This is a configuration toggle (not a Google-issued credential) that enables the inline Drive file picker flow, which lets users grant the app access to specific Drive files without a full re-authentication. To obtain or configure this value, contact your Arcade account setup or check your deployment's environment configuration—this is not issued by Google's developer console but is set within the Arcade platform itself.

For general guidance on configuring secrets in Arcade, see the [Arcade secrets documentation](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets). You can also manage secrets directly at [https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets).
